newsitem.title: SPAIN: U.S. demand for scrap copper seen buoyant.
newsitem.headline: U.S. demand for scrap copper seen buoyant.

text.p: Demand for scrap copper in the U.S. was strong in 1996, and this year is shaping up to be equally buoyant, Michael Casey, vice-president Metal Commodities Inc, said.

Last year scrap was tight in the U.S. and spreads to COMEX copper narrowed, with scrap moving to a premium at one stage. Some SX-EW (solvent extraction electrowon) cathodes were used to meet scrap contracts.
"1997 has begun with good demand and spreads, and at the current pace it should be another good year," Casey said on Tuesday at Metal Bulletin's 10th International Copper Conference.
Although there competition to copper scrap from some SX-EW cathodes, its market share was holding up comparatively well.
"It is evident that scrap has a large share of the U.S. copper market, and I expect to see the scrap market share remain in the 37 percent to 40 percent area during 1997," Casey said.
In 1990, scrap accounted for 44.5 percent of the U.S. market, but declined to 37.5 percent in 1996.
Casey said this partly reflected new mine production, as well as additional SX-EW cathodes. Standard SX-EW cathode competes on a price basis with bare bright copper scrap.

"Off grade cathode, while not deliverable to the Comex or London Metal Exchange (LME) warehouses finds its way to the market and competes with copper scrap to some degree, which might account for the lower scrap market share in recent years," Casey said.
